items.t: Symptoms of allergic rhinitis (including persistent allergic rhinitis) and urticaria, in adults and children aged 6 years and over.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK SmPC accessed.

items.t: Adults and adolescents 12 years and over: 5 mg (1 tablet) once daily.

src.q: Adults and adolescents 12 years and above: The daily recommended dose is 5 mg (1 film-coated tablet).

items.t: Intermittent allergic rhinitis: stop when symptoms clear and restart when they return. Persistent allergic rhinitis: continuous use can be offered during allergen exposure.

src.q: it can be stopped once the symptoms have disappeared and can be restarted again when symptoms reappear
continuous therapy can be proposed to the patient during the period of exposure to allergens

items.t: Elderly: adjust the dose if moderate to severe renal impairment (see renal).

src.q: Adjustment of the dose is recommended in elderly patients with moderate to severe renal impairment

items.t: Children 6-12 years: 5 mg (1 tablet) once daily. Tablets are not recommended under 6 years (no suitable dose); use a paediatric formulation.

src.q: Children aged 6 to 12 years: The daily recommended dose is 5 mg (1 film-coated tablet).
The use of the film-coated tablet formulation is not recommended in children aged less than 6 years
It is recommended to use a paediatric formulation of levocetirizine

items.t: Children with renal impairment: adjust individually by renal clearance and weight; no specific data.

src.q: There are no specific data for children with renal impairment.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to levocetirizine, cetirizine, hydroxyzine, any other piperazine derivative or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance, to cetirizine, to hydroxyzine, to any other piperazine derivatives or to any of the other excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: End-stage renal disease with eGFR below 15 ml/min (requiring dialysis).

src.q: Patients with end stage renal disease with estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) below 15 ml/min (requiring dialysis treatment).

items.t: Caution if predisposed to urinary retention (e.g. spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia).

src.q: Caution should be taken in patients with predisposing factors of urinary retention (e.g. spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia) as levocetirizine may increase the risk of urinary retention.

items.t: Caution in epilepsy and in patients at risk of convulsions: may aggravate seizures.

src.q: Caution should be taken in patients with epilepsy and patients at risk of convulsion as levocetirizine may cause seizure aggravation.

items.t: Contains lactose: patients with galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take it.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total - lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: Precaution with alcohol.

src.q: Precaution is recommended with concurrent intake of alcohol

items.t: Itching may occur after stopping, sometimes intense enough to need restarting treatment.

src.q: Pruritus may occur when levocetirizine is stopped even if those symptoms were not present before treatment initiation.

items.t: Alcohol or other CNS depressants: may further reduce alertness and performance in sensitive patients.

src.q: In sensitive patients, the concurrent administration of cetirizine or levocetirizine and alcohol or other CNS depressants may cause additional reductions in alertness and impairment of performance.

items.t: No interaction studies with levocetirizine. Studies with cetirizine showed no clinically relevant interactions with azithromycin, diazepam, erythromycin, ketoconazole or pseudoephedrine, among others.

src.q: No interaction studies have been performed with levocetirizine

studies with the racemate compound cetirizine demonstrated that there were no clinically relevant adverse interactions (with antipyrine, azithromycin, cimetidine, diazepam, erythromycin, glipizide, ketoconazole and pseudoephedrine)

items.t: Dose interval by eGFR: 60 ml/min or more: 1 tablet once daily; 30 to under 60: 1 tablet every 2 days; 15 to under 30 (not on dialysis): 1 tablet every 3 days; under 15 (on dialysis): contraindicated.

src.q: The dosing intervals must be individualised according to renal function (eGFR - estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate).
Moderately decreased renal function 30 - < 60 1 tablet once every 2 days
Severely decreased renal function 15 - < 30 (not requiring dialysis) 1 tablet once every 3 days
End stage renal disease (ESRD) < 15 (requiring dialysis treatment) Contra-indicated

items.t: Hepatic impairment alone: no dose change. Hepatic plus renal impairment: adjust as for renal impairment.

src.q: No dose adjustment is needed in patients with solely hepatic impairment.
In patients with hepatic impairment and renal impairment, adjustment of the dose is recommended

items.t: SmPC: limited levocetirizine data, but large cetirizine data show no malformations or fetal/neonatal toxicity; may be considered in pregnancy if necessary.

src.q: The use of levocetirizine may be considered during pregnancy, if necessary.
There are no or limited amount of data (less than 300 pregnancy outcomes) from the use of levocetirizine in pregnant women.

items.t: SmPC: likely to pass into breast milk; infant adverse effects possible; use with caution. (The SPS antihistamine breastfeeding page does not cover levocetirizine.)

src.q: Therefore, the excretion of levocetirizine in human milk is likely.
Adverse reactions associated with levocetirizine may be observed in breastfed infants.
caution should be exercised when prescribing levocetirizine to lactating women

items.t: Fertility: no clinical data for levocetirizine.

src.q: For levocetirizine no clinical data are available.

items.t: Common (adults and adolescents): somnolence (5.2% vs 1.4% placebo), headache, dry mouth, fatigue. Uncommon: asthenia, abdominal pain.

items.t: Psychiatric effects including aggression, agitation, depression and suicidal ideation (frequency not known).
